dedupe_keys.name: dyntapy dynamic and static traffic assignment in python

description: dyntapy is a Python package from KU Leuven for macroscopic modelling of car traffic. It extracts and formats road network graphs from OpenStreetMap through OSMnx, parses road network and travel demand inputs, computes shortest paths quickly, runs both static and dynamic traffic assignment algorithms, supports selected link analysis and offers visualisation tools. Its object-oriented definitions of network, demand and results are generic, so further assignment algorithms can be added and the same visualisation used for all of them. It was written by Paul Ortmann and Chris Tampère of the ITSCreaLab. Coverage is generic: any road network that can be taken from OpenStreetMap or parsed from other sources. Access: free on PyPI (version 0.2.4, June 2023) and GitLab, with documentation on Read the Docs and archived versions on Zenodo; the licence is GPL family (Zenodo lists AGPL-3.0 and PyPI lists GPLv3). Caveats: releases stopped in 2023, and it models cars only. It supports network flow and congestion modelling, rerouting after link closures in disruption studies and teaching of traffic assignment, and complements OSMnx and the Transportation Networks for Research test networks catalogued here.
